findings.quote: | a verdict receipt names another revision | refused unless its bytes equal the certified revision on the declared `--paths` surface | `RECEIPT_REV_MISMATCH` |  ...  | a positive control was scored at the freeze | refused: the freeze predates the work it certifies and drifts on the frozen surface | `RECEIPT_REV_CONTENT_DRIFT` (no `--paths`: `RECEIPT_REV_MISMATCH`) |
findings.why: The table keys its refusal codes to the receipt's ROLE, but tools/receipt-revision-gate.py selects the code by whether `--paths` was declared and whether the named surface drifted; the roles take one branch. Measured at C0 on the real round-54 receipt, the same bytes give byte-identical codes as role=verdict and as role=positive: with the declared --paths surface the code is RECEIPT_REV_CONTENT_DRIFT, and without --paths it is RECEIPT_REV_MISMATCH. So row 1's code cell (RECEIPT_REV_MISMATCH) is not what a verdict receipt naming another revision yields on the declared --paths surface that row 1's own rule cell names, and row 2's parenthetical '(no --paths: RECEIPT_REV_MISMATCH)' shows the --paths axis is the real one. The lane's own sourced entry says the same: corpus/knowledge/receipt-revision-binding.md:34 'identical to `positive` (the code takes the two roles in one branch)'. A reader who gates a verdict receipt on a drifted surface and expects RECEIPT_REV_MISMATCH (row 1) sees RECEIPT_REV_CONTENT_DRIFT and will misread the refusal. The round-56 C2 counter gates the very same receipt as role=positive with --paths and expects RECEIPT_REV_CONTENT_DRIFT (arm red54), so the counter and the page disagree about which situation carries which code. Rows 3 and 4 were re-measured and hold: a control set naming an absent revision is refused RECEIPT_REV_UNRESOLVABLE, and a receipt naming no revision at all is refused RECEIPT_REV_ABSENT.

findings.quote: Measured on every documented allocating mode — the seven self-tests plus `env-diff --contract` and `registry-check --rev` — as one stderr line, `<tool>: could-not-evaluate: cannot create clone scratch under the scratch root: TMPDIR is not a usable directory: '<value>' (could-not-evaluate)`, exit 2
findings.why: The quoted byte-shape is not what three of the nine modes it names print. The prefix of the line is the tool's own token, and for bash-witness-study and env-diff that token is not the tool's name: 'WITNESS_STUDY:' and 'ENVDIFF_SETUP:' respectively. A reader who matches the line by the tool's name breaks on 3 of the 9 modes (bash-witness-study selftest, env-diff --selftest, env-diff --contract). The class half of the rule holds 9/9 - every mode exits 2 with exactly one stderr line, no RuntimeError and no Traceback token, and the value is named - so this is a defect of the quoted shape only, not of the tools. The same shape is quoted in the frozen note corpus/knowledge/scratch-root-contract.md ('One line, every mode (round 55)'), which the page cites in the same breath. The lane has already adjudicated the identical defect in the sibling artifact the page cites: round-55's adjudication W2-TOOLDIFF-F3 accepted that 'the seven registry cells quoted <tool>.py while repeat-control prints repeat-control:, bash-witness prints WITNESS_STUDY: and env-diff prints ENVDIFF_SETUP: - 4/7 cells false' and fixed each cell to quote the token its tool actually prints. The registry cells at C0 are fixed (repeat-control:, WITNESS_STUDY:, pin-disposition.py:, evidence-disposition.py:, context-capture.py:, registry-check:, ENVDIFF_SETUP:); this page's copy of the shape was not fixed. Same finding round 55's wave-2 reader filed at r55's C0 (T55W2Read01 finding 1); never landed, because round 55 was rejected-harmed.

IMPROVEMENT (not a finding): the page quotes the gate as 'tools/receipt-revision-gate.py --lane LANE --certified REV', but that form alone exits 1 with a usage error - '--receipt PATH:ROLE[:REGEX]' is mandatory. The complete form is in corpus/knowledge/receipt-revision-binding.md and in the registry cell. Naming the full form (or pointing at the note) would save a reader the usage error.

IMPROVEMENT (not a finding): at C0 the registry carries EIGHT rows with a 'scratch_root' cell, not seven - the seventh tool rows plus the new 'receipt-revision-gate-selftest' row added by the C0 commit itself. The page's 'the seven registry scratch_root cells' is right in the sense the counter measures (the seven tools that call strict_scratch_root(); the round-55 C2 counter's docs arm at C0 reads docs=7/7), but a reader grepping registry.json for scratch_root at C0 counts eight. Worth naming the scope explicitly.

IMPROVEMENT (not a finding): the page's scratch-root bullet says 'the seven self-tests plus env-diff --contract and registry-check --rev' - nine allocating modes - which matches corpus/knowledge/scratch-root-contract.md's nine-mode list and the round-55 counter's 9/9 grammar arm at C0. Correct as written; no change needed.

OBSERVATION (lane-level, outside this section): the census validator exits 0 as required, but the tameshi row count is 142 at C0, not 141: the C0 commit added TWO source rows (S281 and S282) to the 140 present at base 981c5e8b. Flagged for the L1, not filed against this section.

OBSERVATION (not a finding): 'PROVINCE.md declares a write surface' - the file declares ownership and write scope in other words but never uses the phrase 'write surface'. The rule is about a declaration existing, not about a phrase, so nothing in the tree contradicts it; the same judgement was made by round 55's reader (T55W2Read01 item 4c).

PROVENANCE: no SKILL.md, corpus, tools, registry or evidence file was edited by this seat, and no git or jj mutation was run anywhere; every read was 'git show' / 'git grep' / 'git ls-tree' at a named revision, and the only writes are this report, its .md and the receipts directory under .ufo/waves/round-56/w2/. No tool was installed or upgraded.
